priorities.finding: The request-context group is the only positive training-only candidate, with primary lift 0.00221 and full coverage. Its within-user ranking signal is stronger on GAUC for cold users (0.654) than warm users/items (0.631), while nDCG@5 is weaker for cold users (0.492 versus 0.508), indicating useful broad ranking discrimination but limited top-five concentration in that segment.
priorities.recommended_action: Advance only request_context to the next controlled experiment, with daily and segment-level monitoring. Do not expand the feature budget until the positive lift is replicated beyond the internal temporal holdout.

metric_diagnosis: Stop further screening and reject all non-request-context groups. User-profile evidence is slightly negative overall and unstable by day; affinity, recency, duration, and item metadata are negative, with metadata also weakening GAUC. Historical author/item response features are consistently and materially negative in warm-user-and-item GAUC (about 0.467), so they do not provide stable within-user ranking evidence. The request-context lift is modest and daily variability is high, and its cold-item segment is uninformative (GAUC 0.5 on only 8 rows); therefore treat it as a provisional candidate rather than a confirmed win. Exclude current-impression outcomes and quarantine aggregate snapshots because their availability would create leakage.
